title: NVIDIA Vera CPUs land at Los Alamos to power three new future supercomputers
key_facts: Los Alamos National Laboratory has received its first NVIDIA Vera CPU systems, installed in the lab's Darwin testbed for early performance testing.
The node is an air-cooled MGX server with two Vera CPUs, each with 88 Olympus cores, linked by NVIDIA's NVLink Chip-to-Chip connection.
The hardware arrived in August; the Darwin team, supported by the NNSA's Advanced Simulation and Computing Program, installed it and testing followed once the software was deployed.
It is a forerunner of three planned Los Alamos supercomputers, Mission, Vision and Veritas, which will use Vera CPUs together with NVIDIA Rubin GPUs.
Mission will have three partitions: Ranger (Vera CPUs), Sandstone (Vera Rubin NVL-4) and Starlight (Vera Rubin NVL-72); Vera CPU nodes are also planned for Veritas.
The full Ranger partition is expected in 2027 alongside Sandstone; the Mission-Starlight and Vision-Transformer partitions could arrive as early as late 2026.
The earlier Grace CPU powers the lab's Venado supercomputer, built by NVIDIA and HPE.
